name: Funding-contrarian crash filter — fade crowded-long funding extremes
rationale: Perpetual funding is a crowding gauge: an EXTREME positive rate means longs are paying a steep premium to shorts — the book is lopsided, leverage is stacked on the long side, and the marginal buyer is exhausted. That is the precondition for a long-squeeze / liquidation cascade: a small down-move forces leveraged longs to sell, which feeds on itself. This family is the contrarian fade of that crowded-long extreme — a SHORT (direction -1) entered ONLY when (a) funding is above a fitted EXTREME floor (crowded, not merely positive — distinct from funding-carry, which harvests mild positive carry on the long side), (b) price has run up over the trend window (a stretched top, not a fresh breakout), and (c) realized vol is below a fitted ceiling so we are fading euphoria, not knife-catching an already-crashing tape. Exit when funding normalizes back below a fitted reset floor (the crowd has de-levered — the edge is gone) or the stop/TP fires. This is the documented funding-spike-before-crash pattern (crowded-leverage mean-reversion); it is the inverse of the carry trade and complements it. No magic numbers — every threshold lives in param_space and is fit by the Finder grid.
catalyst: Extreme positive perpetual funding = crowded-long leverage paying a steep premium; the squeeze/cascade that unwinds it is faded with a short.
